chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Ali from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the going out of women on the two Eids and for Friday prayer, so he said, 'Except for an elderly woman.'

key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: The two Eid festivals (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on women attending Friday and Eid prayers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a general prohibition for women attending Eid prayers and Friday congregational prayers, citing the principle of preserving modesty and minimizing fitnah. The exception for 'elderly women' (al-musinnah) reflects the scholarly view that their established presence and reduced likelihood of attracting undue attention make their participation permissible, highlighting the balance between religious obligation and social context in Shia fiqh.
